title: Anchored release chooser and profile publish wizard
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Enable a guided, auditable flow in the Console for selecting a specific model version (anchoring/pinning), previewing the version's published performance profile, running a simulated traffic split, and publishing the profile with an optional rollout schedule. This ticket scopes the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and implementation handoff for the UX wizard that reduces accidental pinning, surfaces perf regressions, and ensures auditability for enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Console exposes a ‘Choose anchor’ modal that lists model family versions with sortable performance metrics (p50 latency, median cost/token, recent eval score) and clear indicators for compatibility and quantization variants.
Users can open a side-by-side diff between candidate version performance profiles (baseline vs candidate) and filter diffs by workload (chat, completion, embeddings).

The wizard includes a traffic-split simulator where PMs/devs can preview latency and cost impact for 0-100% traffic distribution and schedule a staged rollout (canary -> ramp -> pinned) with time windows.
Publishing a profile creates a traceable audit event with who/when/notes and links to the published profile snapshot and related PR/Spec.
If a profile includes quantized variants or fallback models, UI surfaces the fallback mapping and the automatic fallback policy rule linked to the deployment.
UI provides inline warnings when the selected version has recent regression alerts or unresolved quality regressions and requires an explicit acknowledgment before publishing.
End-to-end flow covered by a small e2e test harness (console E2E) and a design QA checklist; product owners can demonstrate the flow against staging in the demo script.

decisions: Expose version-level metrics that are read-only in the chooser; detailed metric time ranges default to 7d with user override.
Make publishing an explicit two-step action: 'Publish profile (draft -> publish)' with required acknowledgement if regressions exist.
Traffic simulator will use sampled production p95/p50 latency baselines and a cost model backed by Optimize recommendations to estimate cost delta.
We will not allow cross-model-family pinning in the initial release — only version variants within the same family.
Audit events will be retained for 365 days and exportable as CSV from the Console audit log page.
